classification.difficultyReason: Count black objects and total objects in the supplied ball and card representations, using the response scaffold.

content.prompt: Calculate the probability of these events.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 1a, bucket to the left of the count and fraction scaffolds
spec.description: Outlined bucket, curved handle and grip, elliptical opening and oval window containing ten separate balls in the source-relative arrangement.
spec.mathematics: Three black, three blue, three white and one orange ball; ten outcomes in total.
spec.answerVisibility: All balls are permanent question givens. No counts or probability answers are printed on the diagram.

answer.worked:
There are $3$ black balls among $10$ balls.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{black ball})&=\frac{\text{number of black balls}}{\text{total number of balls}}\\P(\text{black ball})&=\frac{3}{10}\end{align*}$$
The boxes contain $3$, $3$ and $10$, in order.

answer.worked:
There are $5$ black cards among $8$ cards.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{black card})&=\frac{\text{number of black cards}}{\text{total number of cards}}\\P(\text{black card})&=\frac{5}{8}\end{align*}$$
The boxes contain $8$, $5$ and $8$, in order.
